utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We briefly move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have just one brief preliminary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would that -- one second. Can the witness already be --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, one second. We are back in open session. Mr. File, should that --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: It doesn't affect whether the witness is here or not so we can bring the witness in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then the witness can be brought in. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: On 12th of August, 2015, at transcript 37.719 to 37.722, Mr. Lukic of the Defence raised an issue related to the English translation of a Prosecution exhibit, P1147, specifically it related to page 94 of the English translation, line 19 of that page. We verified the translation and we now have a revised translation of that page. We discussed this with Mr. Lukic and the parties have agreed that the revised translation page should replace what is currently page 94 of the English translation of P1147. We've uploaded the revised page as 65 ter number 28780a [Realtime transcript read in error "28680a"], and we would ask that are that replacement to be made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which would mean that the original page is taken out of that document or have you uploaded the entire new version, including that one corrected page.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I believe it's just the one corrected page. I note the transcript reads in error 28680a. The correct number is 28780a and it would just be to replace that one page in the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, that causes no problems to replace one page from a document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, it should not, Your Honours. It will be implemented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you are hereby instructed to replace the page 94 of P1147 by the new one uploaded by the Prosecution. Good morning, Ms. Radovanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As always, I'd like to remind that you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony. And Mr. File will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. File, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Now, before we return to the hypothetical case we were looking at yesterday afternoon, I just want to cover one discrete issue with you. First, when the ICMP makes a final and conclusive DNA identification, you do not dispute the accuracy of that identification; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did not have any occasion to dispute the accuracy, but I have a problem with it. The problem is that when the ICMP provides a table, nobody signs it and we don't know who is responsible for the content of the table.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: That's actually my question. The content itself of the table, you don't dispute that regarding the identification.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in a position to dispute it. I never had an opportunity to compare what they gave to Dr. Tabeau and what I requested from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accept -- I accept it as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. In your report at paragraphs 48 and 49, you criticise Dr. Tabeau for counting as separate individuals the 22 people whose DNA identifications were still under review or were not identified by the ICMP by June 2014. Do you recall that criticism that you made?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay, I don't --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say that -- please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The only thing what asked whether you recall that. You've answered that question. Next question, please, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: When Dr. Tabeau was testifying at T36.728, she said: "They are unique, different, unique individuals in terms of DNA profiles and different from all other individuals with certain DNA profiles under the main cases." So even if at that time we didn't know who they were, we still knew that they were unique individuals distinct from those who had already been identified, so there is no problem with including them in the count of individuals recovered from Tomasica, is there?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it that way. The ICMP, in their letter, say precisely: Regarding 15 persons, it is probable that they have been matched on the basis of DNA. Probable is not certain. Concerning seven persons, they say precisely they have not been matched --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- with the family.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Would you consider it relevant for the sake of your report to know if these individuals had actually been conclusively identified since June 2014?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if I take the word of Dr. Tabeau. I don't have any document to support it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ICMP did not send me a letter that they have done that. Or maybe I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: When you came to The Hague in January 2016, did you ask to look at the most recent ICMP update from Tomasica, which was from October 2015?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be honest, I don't remember now. But I believe I requested all ICMP reports. Whether there was one from October 2015, I can't remember. But I have seen that correction, and that correction contains tables showing how Dr. Tabeau corrected some things, but not ICMP tables, as far as I recall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File, could I take you back three questions, when you asked about the unique 22 persons, did you consider the answer given by the expert witness an answer to your question? Because then I might have misunderstood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: No, I -- I don't see that as a direct answer to my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, if you ask that question, if you get an answer which is not an answer to your question, I think for this Chamber it would be important to at least establish that. And either seek an answer or to establish that no answer was given in order to avoid any confusion on our part.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I ask this, because when Mr. File asked you about the 22 unique individuals, you started talking about that there was for 15 there was a probable match, for 7, there was no match. The question was not about matches. The question was whether these 22 were distinct from all the others who had been identified, and, therefore, your answer may be fully correct but was not an answer to the question. Please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could we look at P7437, which is actually going to be on Sanction because it's an Excel spreadsheet. This is the June 2014 ICMP file on DNA identifications of Tomasica victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And while we're looking at it, you can see in the second -- in the -- in the column to the left -- no, the second column from the left, the names of the individuals and how their main cases and reassociation identifications are grouped together, which was what we were looking at yesterday regarding the non-sequential ID numbering of identified victims. Now, if you look at the bottom of this page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File, is this to be shown publicly.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Sorry. This is not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: If you look at the bottom of the page, this tab is called: Submitted DNA report. Now, if we go to the second tab which is called: DNA reports review, here you see there are 15 main cases along with their reassociations that were under review at that time. The main cases are at rows 2 to 7, 11 to 15, 18, and 20 to 22. And then if we look at tab 3, titled: No match, you see seven main cases in blue under source case ID along with reassociations in red in the next column that had no match in June 2014? Now, if we can switch to 65 ter number 33792, which is the October 2015 spreadsheet. First of all, what you'll notice is there's no tab 2 for review at the bottom. And if we scroll down what you see is what was previously tab 2. They've been identified with yellow boxes as newly identified cases. Now, if we look at the second tab for no match, we see there's only one source case ID or main case that is remaining unidentified along with its reassociations. So now that you know that all but one person from Tomasica has been conclusively identified as of October of last year, would you modify your conclusions about whether to treat those newly identified individuals as unique, separate Tomasica victims?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will object to the question until we find out when this was disclosed to the Defence, this document that dates from October 2015.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: It was disclosed on 21st of October, 2015 in batch 124.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, does your objection stand or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That was just to get the information so he can ask the question now. I don't think the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it -- as a matter of fact, it wasn't an objection to the question, I think, but you wanted to raise a disclosure issue related to the question put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Related to the document put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Do you remember the question I just asked?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, but before I answer, may I ask you to put back the previous table once again. Because I can't follow it now. It switches very quickly. The table before no match, the one you just showed me, saying the non-identified -- or the newly identified ones are marked in yellow. Yes, I see it now. I would not change anything because Dr. Tabeau has already included these people in her report. And my objection is why? In her calculation, technically nothing changed. She has already included them in her total.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: But then to go back to your answer that we were discussing before, when I asked you about the fact that these were unique identifications that simply had not been confirmed at that point or matched at that point but they were unique profiles, your response was there it was only probably matched to an identity. But you don't dispute that they were unique DNA profiles; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't dispute it, but I don't know what unique is understood to mean. A unique DNA profile doesn't mean anything to me unless you explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could we switch back to e-court and look at 65 ter 33791, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But before we do so, do I understand that you do not know the understanding of the word "unique"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know what the word "unique" means, but I don't know what the Prosecutor understands under that term. If he believes that a unique profile is the fact that somebody was later identified as such, all right. But you can have several unique DNA profiles, if you have more than one part, based on which you look for a DNA profile. My impression is that the Prosecutor understands a unique DNA profile to be equivalent to an exhumed person. If that's what the Prosecutor believes, then I would say that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. My understanding, and let's check whether that is also the understanding of the Prosecution, my understanding of a unique DNA profile is a profile which differs from other known profiles. That makes it unique because it's not the same as any of the other ones known. And that's how we started in the beginning, where you gave an answer - not an answer to the question - when the Prosecutor asked you, we had a lot of identified DNA profiles. There were 22 where there was no match, but what was put to you by the Prosecution at that time was that those 22, 15 of them were the probable match, 7 not with a match. That at least there they were unique in the sense that those 22 were all different among each other and also different from those where a match had been confirmed. That was the question at the time, whether these are unique persons, that is, persons with a different DNA profile. That's how I understood your questions, Mr. File. Could you now please perhaps answer the first question that was put to you, whether you agree that those 22 are unique profiles, that is, different from any other profile known in this context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that's the way you explained it, then, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could we look at 65 ter number 33791, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And as this comes up, my follow-up question to your answer would be: If you accept that they were unique DNA profiles, then your criticism of Dr. Tabeau for counting them as separate individuals does not stand; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If they are proven unique DNA profile, then that critique doesn't stand but I'm saying again it doesn't change anything to the total because they have been already counted among the victims of Tomasica.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I may have a technical difficulty with our screen for e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have a black screen at this moment. Mr. Registrar, any way to -- now I see text again. B/C/S to the left; English to the right. An overview of the 2015 ICMP update on the Tomasica identified, dated 24th of November, 2015; author, apparently Ewa Tabeau. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: When you were drafting the part of your report that we are discussing now, did you see or had you seen this report drafted by Ewa Tabeau which was disclosed to the Defence on the 27th of November, 2015 and which further describes the results of the update we were just looking at?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be sincere, I don't remember. I believe I've seen all the reports but I really can't remember whether I've seen this one, in particular. But the fact is that it's about the same number of people that Dr. Tabeau states in her conclusion. I have probably read it because I've read thousands of pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me draw your attention to just a few sections of this. Paragraph 1 at the beginning, it says: "In this research note, I summarise the October 2015 ICMP update on the DNA identification of the persons buried in the Tomasica mine, Prijedor municipality, Bosnia and Herzegovina. This note does not expand on or make any changes to my 2014 expert report on Tomasica but merely gives the latest figures on the DNA identification process of these individuals." If we go to paragraph 2, starting with the third sentence. It says: "The 15 main cases listed in 2014 without any personal information are now complete, i.e., they have names and dates of birth (DOBs). One person was reported in 2014 exclusively on the basis of his associated reports, i.e., without a main case which was corrected in the 2015 update. This means that also this corrected case can be counted as an additional person. Altogether, 23 new fully complete main cases have been added since June 2014. (Annex 1)." So if you had read this, and you were criticizing Dr. Tabeau for including these individuals as separate individuals, would this have not factored into your decision to issue that criticism?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence will object to the use of this document and the presentation of material from this document. This document is a report authored by the expert witness of the Prosecution. This report was not disclosed under Rule 94 bis as a report that was being relied upon at trial. The Prosecution reopened its case to call Ms. Tabeau in July of 2015. Thereafter, they've re-closed their case. Now, we're having a new report from the expert witness that has not gone through the procedures that this Court has set forth for expert reports. So they can't now, again, for a second time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There's probably no translation in B/C/S from either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that from two sides we hear that there's no interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now we do, apparently. So the Prosecution cannot be permitted now a second time to amend or add on to evidence of their expert witness outside of the rules and decisions that have been set forth to permit that. By trying to get this report in, in this manner, the Prosecution is basically violating the order on reopening and is violating Rule 94 bis and so the Defence would ask for Your Honours to issue a ruling on that matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe this objection is premature. I'm not tendering this document right now, and I believe I have every right to explore with this witness the information she had available to her when drafting her critique and what she chose to accept or ignore is relevant for this Chamber to know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Understanding that you're not tendering this document, Mr. File, it will not be admitted then in evidence and you may put the information in this -- contained in this document to the witness while examining her. In that respect, I don't know whether, Mr. Ivetic, whether your objection was against presenting new evidence or putting this to the witness, but at least the Chamber, in response to what you raised, allows Mr. File to put this information to the witness as information she says she most likely has seen and is relevant for the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if it is being entered into the record that is precisely a back-doorway of getting material into evidence, so I fail to see the difference between whether a report is being tendered or not. If it is being used with a witness in court on the record and the material is being provided to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I see it as essentially the same thing, so I have to say the Defence views it as still a violation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That objection is denied. This witness may have had access to this material. She may have considered it when answering the questions. Therefore, it may be put to her. It was disclosed TO THE Defence. Not -- not as evidence but just to hear her response to what Mr. File asks her and that's my ruling. Mr. File, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So I'm just going to return to the question that I asked you, which was: If you had read this and you were criticizing Dr. Tabeau for including these individuals as separate individuals, would this not have factored into your decision to issue that criticism?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object to the form of the question. The form of the question is relating to Professor Radovanovic's conclusions in her report which relate to the evidence that was admitted by Dr. Tabeau. So trying to link that conclusion to material that is not in evidence is now, again, going beyond the scope of the evidence that was presented via Ms. Tabeau that Professor Radovanovic was asked to comment upon in an expert manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Objection is denied. It's relevant for the -- it's relevant for the testimony which is evidence of this witness to put this information to her. Please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Can you answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I would change anything, except perhaps that she is putting in what doesn't even exist yet at the time she is writing the report. But it doesn't change the whole total. Dr. Tabeau made new calculations every year. If I had been receiving that month by month, then it would have been all right. She has another correction, I believe, from 2015, to the total number that I have seen here in The Hague, but that's a correction to the total number, and now she says it is no longer 378 but it's -- so these corrections Dr. Tabeau is making here now do not affect the overall result. Because --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, just let me finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... thank you. I think have you answered the question: It would not change your conclusions. Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We're going to return to the simplified hypothetical that we looked at yesterday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: If we can put that on Sanction again.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Just a few more questions about this and then we're going to dive into a real-world case.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I think we need to switch to Sanction. Oh. I have a black screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have a list of students registered for this class.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps it's just my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The Defence also has apparently what Your Honours see.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Well, I have it on a different screen so I can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So when we left off, we had match -- we can go forward a few slides to the matches that we had made. There we go. We had matched the student exams with the class registration list. Assisted in part by some of the student IDs as you pointed out. So regarding the accuracy and the completeness of the data fields in the exams, in this example, we had first name, middle name, last name, and student ID. So four pieces of data for each student exam, meaning 20 different pieces of data in total that you could potentially have used to make matches. Now, assuming for the moment that your registration list is correct, if we can go to the next slide. And one more. So for the first exam you received there are zero complete and accurate fields, because the first name is incomplete, missing the middle name and the last name and probably the wrong ID. For the second, there's one complete and accurate field. The first name is inaccurate since he appears to be using a nickname. Middle name is missing, last name is correct, but the ID number is incomplete. For the third exam, there are two complete and accurate fields. Correct first name, missing middle name and last name, and correct ID. For the fourth exam, there are zero complete and accurate fields because it's missing the first name, misspelled the middle name, missing the last name and missing the ID. And for John Douglas Smith, 124, all four data fields are correct and accurate. Now, if we go to the next slide. So in this exam data source, out of 20 data fields, seven are present, correct and complete, while 13 are missing or incorrect or incomplete, which would give us a rate of accuracy of 35 per cent or a rate of error or incompleteness of 65 per cent; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be frank, I do not understand what you want, nor do I understand how you computed these percentages and what you're trying to ask me and what I'm supposed to explain here. I don't know how you computed that seven of 20 are correct. Seven of what? Of the elements that we have here? Do you -- I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me, as a layperson, let me try to tell you how I understand that as a layperson. That accurate and complete data fields if you add to zero for the first one, 1 for the second, 2 for the third, zero for the fourth and four for number five, then if you add all that you come to seven. And as Mr. File explained before, in total, there would have been 20 data fields which are known for the comparative group, which means seven accurate fields where there could have been 20, seven out of 20 is 35 and therefore would be 35 per cent. That's how I understand it. Mr. File, is my understanding correct? Would you -- have you now followed me in what seven means, what 20 means, and what 35 per cent would mean? Apart from just numbers. So I'm not yet interpreting anything, but ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have understood how you have -- how you understood it, but I don't understand it in the same way. Because in statistics or in demographics this is not done in that way. If you take these as characteristics, first and last name, father's name and the ID element, and you control all the names and you say of the five names, all five are 100 per cent correct, but you never control in this way. You're controlling in quite a different way when the sources of data are checked: each element has to be checked separately rather than in this way. Because how would you know how many fields are filled in terms of date of birth unless you check all the dates of birth in your source and you can say of the 22.000, as registered by ICRC, 50 per cent of the fields for date of birth are filled, 25 per cent partially filled. And the remaining percentage is missing the data. That's how you check it. So what the Prosecutor is showing me, the checking is not used in this way in the matching process. For this, I could say, correspondence of name, 100 per cent. One, 2, 3, 4, 5, no correspondence with father's name and 100 per cent of correspondence with the last names. In the source provided by doctor. Provided by the Prosecutor. ID numbers different, so I can try to locate them on the basis of ID numbers, but Dr. Tabeau can not look for that in her sources because ICRC, for example, does not provide ID numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not yet at Dr. Tabeau. We are just taking this and the question is: Do you understand now the calculation as made by Mr. File. He has not in any way yet linked it to whether Dr. Tabeau had the same data available. That's a different matter. Please proceed, Mr. File. I see that the witness was nodding yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't put it right. I could check whether all the ID numbers are 100 per cent correct, if I had another source with ID numbers. That's how you check the data source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And as you know, this is just a hypothetical so that's why we're focussing just on the information that we have here. Now, this is probably a common sense question, but there's a reason that you would not try to match the student exams with the registration list of the entire school because if you tried to match it with the whole school, you could increase the risk of creating some bad matches, like perhaps the real student number 126 who is not taking your class might get matched with John Elliot Smith's exam just because Elliot wrote the wrong student ID number on his test. So you would agree that it would be best to limit the matching only to students registered to take your class in this example; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object to the question. There's multiple questions in there. It's a compound question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Well, I just put the premise for the reason and I put to the witness so I'm asking whether she would limit the -- it's not a compound question I'm asking whether she would limit the matching only to the students registered to the class. That's the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: He asked if it would increase the risk and then he asked would it best to limit the matching. Those are two separate questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

The fewer the number of elements, you then have to make calculations. You have to review everything personally to draw some conclusions, to say, yes, it is one and the same person. utterances.text: Let me stop you there. Whatever your task may have been, I'd rather have you answer the question that was put to you by Mr. File. utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's precisely for this point, to say that the witness did answer Mr. File's question as you did later on read [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

In that report, we have 72 criteria, which identify for each criteria the matching that was the result of searching under that criteria. That example is not in relation to their list of victims for Srebrenica. That example is in relation to matching the -- the -- the ICRC list with the 1991 census. We have not been provided, either for the Srebrenica victims nor the Tomasica victims, the results of the actual matching that Dr. Tabeau claims to have undertaken to be able to verify what criteria were used, what criteria were not used. Dr. Tabeau, in answers to my questions, indicated that in addition to the -- to 72 criteria from the Srebrenica report, she also used additional criteria which, to this date, have never been enunciated, defined or given to the Defence by the Prosecution. I have no other way of -- of labelling this activity than to say they are hiding it. And in that regard, I would also ask that they please release a document that telling me to date doesn't exist, which I was given yesterday on their cross-examination list, and that is a document bearing the 65 ter 33826, with the ERN number R068-6874-R068-6874. That document does not appear on EDS under that ERN number.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Ivetic kindly slow down a little, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Slow down a bit and calm down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When I sought this document this morning after realising it was not released in e-court, I was told the document doesn't exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I think the calming down is done perfectly. The slowing down, not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Not yet. Let me try to accommodate both. In relation to this document, I asked for it this morning and was told that this number didn't exist. One minute later, I was given an e-mail with a new document under this number that doesn't fit the description that was disclosed to us yesterday on the cross-examination list, which says: "Table upper with three names as reported by ICRC 2009 and in parallel by the 1991 census in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Summarising the overlap between 1D06189 and the list of 385 cases of DNA-identified persons exhumed from Tomasica in the fall of 2013. "The second table, lower, includes clarifications of inconsistencies in the dates of birth between the ICRC, 2009, and 1991 census for the same three individuals." Why can't the Defence get the documents that they claim to have that they then claim that they don't have. If they relate specifically to objections that have been raised as to the methodology of the report. Why can't the Defence see what Dr. Tabeau relied upon in using her demographic skills to give evidence under oath to this Chamber? I am at a loss as to what is going on here, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So am I, Your Honour. This -- this discussion from Mr. Ivetic refers to a document that I -- I -- it was not on our cross-examination list. We had a number reserved for the document what is currently there which we uploaded this morning. This document is -- that he is referring to, I don't know where he has this reference from, but it's not intended to be used on cross-examination and there's no reason for Defence to be requesting this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Does the document exist? We've been playing cat and mouse trying to get access to documents that they say do exist, don't exist. Does the document exist? If it does, I want it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, not quite unusual that various matters are mixed up at this moment. Mr. Ivetic is talking about disclosure of a document where he wants to know whether it exists or not. Whereas you are talking apparently about a list of documents you wish or do not wish to use during cross-examination. Could you answer the question put by Mr. Ivetic or perhaps in the next break sit together and see what's really bothering both of you, because two people being lost is a serious situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We can certainly discuss it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I would leave it for the time being to that. And I would urge the parties not to mix up all kind of things, that is, identification processes, exactly the way in which it was done, automated, not automated, and verification of the outcome of a process. These are not exactly the same things, and I would urge you not to mix them up. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And, for the record, Your Honour, your interpretation was correct, what we're talking about --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Dr. Radovanovic, just in case you haven't followed all of what we've been discussing, is the verification of the matches that you can see in Dr. Tabeau's Annex 1, for example. So getting back to this table that you produced that's on the screen with the 24 entries, that table does not appear in your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Just for the sake of clarity, you didn't make any of these matches yourself. They're just selected data fields that have been copied and pasted from the demographics unit integrated mortality database; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't do a single one because Dr. Tabeau didn't give me the ICRC from 2005, although I requested that document. And she says she worked based on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: If you'd please just answer the question.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I took that from the integrated database, according to the ICRC, from 2009 and the census.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And your report does not contain any tables of any kind that you produced with your own data matching or your own calculations; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you, I didn't have the 2005 ICRC. I cannot match if I don't have the source that was the basis for her work. If I had had the database, then I maybe would have been able to do something with the 2005 ICRC.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: You -- you had the 2009 ICRC list. You appear to be saying that you chose not to use that one. But if you wanted the 2005 ICRC list, why didn't you ask for it during the week that you were here?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I requested it in writing from the OTP, and they probably forwarded it to Dr. Tabeau. She says, I did my work from -- on the basis of the 2009 ICRC, and then in the document, it is stated that it was all based on the 2005 list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We earlier had a discussion on what was requested in writing or in any other way, and the Chamber would appreciate to it -- that reference is made to the specific requests in writing because earlier we established that sometimes what was considered to be addressed to Dr. Tabeau actually was given to the Defence, and perhaps when the Defence communicated to the Prosecution and then sometimes in different wordings. So in order not for this Chamber to get lost as well, we'd appreciate if any such request is referred to, that we receive or at least are given access to what exactly was asked, by whom, in writing, at what time, and with what formulation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can indicate this was written request number 1 on the list that was given to the Prosecution in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we still haven't seen it. But when was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: It was November 2015.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We had a discussion yesterday that it was either late October, early November. So around that date, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I remember that we had a discussion on that. Again, the formulation, I think, was still somewhat implicit. If you want us to seriously consider that, provide us with that information so that we can look at it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So you still haven't answered my question, which was: If you had wanted, specifically, the 2005 ICRC list and you arrived in January here and you found that you had been given the more recent ICRC list that Dr. Tabeau refers to in her report but you still wanted the 2005 ICRC list, why didn't you ask for it when you were here and you saw that it wasn't among the materials that you had?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I requested it in writing, and I believe that it has not been given to me intentionally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's -- let me there, again, stop you. You asked for something in writing. Two months later, you're in The Hague. You haven't received it. Do I understand your answer well, that you say I didn't again ask for it because I felt already that it was intentionally kept away from me and, therefore, I didn't ask for it again? Is that how we have to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you send something to somebody in writing and if it's on record --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... would you please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any case, I don't think it's accidental.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, not an answer to my question. I invited you now twice to answer my question. You apparently have reasons not to do that. Mr. File, next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Although it's my colleagues business today, Your Honour, I have to object at this moment. How many times the Defence has to ask so that the Prosecution [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not our experts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I cannot tolerate this anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please sit down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you sit down. You sit down and I'll say something you. Please sit down. Mr. Lukic, you do not intervene in an examination of a witness to raise disclosure issues and certainly not if a witness has refused to answer twice or has at least not answered twice a question I put to her. That's not the appropriate moment, not being involved in the examination of the witness at all, that's not the appropriate moment to raise a matter which is about the substance of what I asked. The matter can be raised in re-examination. It was inappropriate to intervene in the way you did, and we will now continue. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Defence takes exception to Your Honours saying that the witness has refused to answer. The witness has attempted to answer on two occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm allowed to make a record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm not. I want a ruling on that. I'm not allowed to make a record. I want a ruling of that. I want it in writing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, on the basis of your first few words, I intervened. I corrected myself when I said the witness refused to answer my question. I said the witness did not answer my question. I corrected myself. Perhaps -- that's clear. That's the reason why I stopped you there, because what I said and what you wanted to rely upon was corrected by myself. And I leave it to that at this moment. We will now continue. Mr. Mladic is thinking that it's time for a break. He is asking for a break. One second, please. No speaking aloud.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not a break. I would like to say something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently Mr. Mladic would like to consult with counsel. He is given an opportunity to do so. At such a volume that it's inaudible for anyone else. Inaudible, I said. Inaudible, I said. Mr. Mladic, if you continue to speak aloud, you're removed -- you'll be removed from this courtroom. Has Mr. Mladic his earphones on? He apparently has not. Mr. Mladic, put on your earphones, please, or, Mr. Lukic, would you please advise Mr. Mladic to put his earphones on. Mr. Mladic, next time, if you consult with counsel, you should speak at a volume inaudible for others, and you should keep on at least one of your earphones so that you can follow the instructions I give you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I may continue and I'll state what I wanted to state before you interrupted me. You cannot -- it is the Defence's position that one cannot say that a witness has failed to answer a question when on both occasions Your Honour interrupted the witness in mid answer. That is creating a fake record, an improper record of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If we would have to wait until the end of the answer of this witness, again and again and again, where she moves away consistently from the questions that are put to you, under those circumstances a Presiding Judge can intervene, and that what's I did. Mr. File your next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So just to clarify that between your report and your testimony, the one piece of work that you've shown us in data tables from the time that you spent here at the Tribunal in January boils down to this one-page table of 24 entries that you copy/pasted from part of the integrated mortality database; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm dealing with what is scientifically established. I don't have to provide tables. I don't deal with numbers. I'm proving that official demographic data is available for that, and Dr. Tabeau hasn't used them. This is not a table that should be used as part of my report because it shows the methodology of matching used by Dr. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Once again, not my question. The question was: Between your report and your testimony, both of them combined, the one piece of work that you've shown us in data tables from the time that you spent here at the Tribunal in January boils down to this one-page table of 24 entries that you copy/pasted from part of the integrated mortality database; right? That is the work that we've seen.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as a proof of matching.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. So then when you spent a week here in The Hague, did you perform any data-matching operations using any of the Demographics Unit resources while you were here, either the ICRC or the integrated mortality database or the ICMP list of missing, or the book of missing from Prijedor municipality? Did you do any data matching at all while you were here?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't need to. And I didn't do that because I did not have the appropriate document from ICRC. And, secondly, I prove in a number of ways that the matching as performed by Dr. Tabeau is not scientifically based. And for that, I don't need tables at all. I can see the quality of the data sources. I see what she is saying. I can see that she uses a special methodology which is inexistent [as interpreted]. I see that she say it's the same as Srebrenica, so I don't need to prove whether she drew the numbers correctly or incorrectly. I'm showing how she is performing the matching and that's it's not scientifically based.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay, I'll take that as a no. Now, one way to verify whether a match is a good match is to see if there are any alternative candidates out there that might be a better match. So if you didn't do any data matching, you didn't compare any of these sources together, you're not able to tell us if there's any better match out there than the one that Dr. Tabeau provides.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not supposed to say that. What I'm supposed to say is what Dr. Tabeau has done, and I say that she did everything on the basis of a methodology which is not practiced anywhere in scientific research.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So then there is something I'm wondering related to your allegations related to combat fatalities. If you're here in The Hague in January, you have the list of 378 identified Tomasica victims, you have access to the ABiH database of fallen soldiers, you've complained that Dr. Tabeau did not use that ABiH list in her analysis, so why didn't you just do it yourself, look for some matches and see what you find? See if there are any Tomasica identified in the ABiH list?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because when you do not use a data source which exists and that's what Dr. Tabeau is doing, she is not using a data source, it is up to me to prove that this is not scientific and not professional. Rather than to prove that there are so many soldiers in Dr. Tabeau's list, I claim that she did not use sources that may that combat did happen. So that's the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... aware of that claim of yours, but what I'm asking you is: Dr. Tabeau did have a source for the Tomasica identified. You had that source too. You could have just looked for those names in the ABiH list, which you had when you were here. But you didn't do that, did you?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I was not the one who was supposed to do it. It was rather, Dr. Tabeau. It was up to her. It is not I who needs to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me interfere again. You said several times yet you don't have to prove anything. Well, first of all, you're here as an expert witness. Proving is -- even the Defence doesn't have to prove anything; It's the Prosecution who has to prove something. I do understand your answer that you thought it to be sufficient to comment on what Dr. Tabeau did, and that's what you did, and that you didn't consider it of any use or of any value to do more than what you did. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My task was to prove whether this is scientifically based. If I proved that she leaves out sources on the basis of which something could be, that's my task. Whether it is scientifically established. And if she leaves out professional sources which exist and which may prove something, it's a proof that she is not applying scientific methodology but modifies it in accordance with her needs. And I'm not disputing any numbers with regard to Dr. Tabeau. She could have done anything she wanted on the basis of the methodology which she applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, if would you have done it, where you say you don't have to, would that not have strengthened, perhaps, the outcome of that, your allegations against Dr. Tabeau, because if you would be able to do it and then demonstrate that Dr. Tabeau didn't do it to serve her own needs, wouldn't that have strengthened your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I did do that, only I don't mention it. I contacted registrars and I know that there are data sources available which are normally used in scientific research but Dr. Tabeau has not done that. She says she used death certificates from the registers of death. There is not a single one in the disclosed... So I did what I believed was my task. And I demonstrated that. It's not true that she is using this and such a source does exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I still do not consider this to be an answer to your question even after five lines. But please put your next question to the witness, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Dr. Radovanovic, when you were a Defence expert witness in the Popovic case, you came to the Tribunal to use some of the same demographics resources; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ones that I requested. Whether they were one and the same I really couldn't tell you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: That was another week-long visit just like in this case. It was from 5 to 10 February 2007. Is that a yes?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And during the time you were here, you matched the OTP list of missing and dead from Srebrenica which had over 7.600 people on it, with the ABiH list of fallen soldiers and you produced a number of lists in annexes to your report in that case with thousands of names that you matched during that visit; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And on that same visit, you performed matching searches in other databases as well and you produced additional annexes for those?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the Defence asked me to do that. That was my task: To check the BA lists and match them with lists from Srebrenica because, up until then, they claimed there were no soldiers in their lists from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So it's something -- on that five-day visit, you matched a OTP list that was about 20 times larger than the Tomasica list here and you produced annexes showing the results. But you're claiming that it just wasn't your job to do it this time?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I say that it wasn't my job. I stated exactly what was the job that I received from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I think we're around the time for a break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are, Mr. File. We take a break, and we'd like to see you back, Ms. Radovanovic, in 20 minutes from now. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at quarter past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see, Mr. Ivetic, that you are on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. To put on the record that, pursuant to your request, we spoke with the Prosecutor during the break. They confirmed that the document which I cited originally in court as 65 ter number 33826, with the stated ERN number of R068-6874 does exist and had not been previously given to the Defence. I have now been given a copy of a document which does not bear the ERN number but which I'm told is that document. I will review the same. But at the same time, Your Honours, the Defence would want to place on the record as we did during the discussions during this break, repeatedly, we have asked the Prosecution for Dr. Tabeau's matching criteria that she used for Tomasica. At our transcript, at transcript page 36.792, Dr. Tabeau said this would take some time but it could be done. To this date, the Defence has not received the same. We would like to draw to Your Honours' attention some case law that indicates -- and this is from the Prosecutor vs Martic, Decision of Prosecution Motions for admission of transcripts pursuant to Rule 92 bis and of expert reports pursuant to Rule 94 bis of 13 January 2006 at paragraph 37. It is also from the Gotovina case, Decision on Disclosure of Expert Materials, 27 August 2009. And it reads as follows: "An expert is expected to give his or her expert opinion in full transparency of the established or assumed facts that he or she relies upon and on the methods used when applying his or her knowledge, experience or skills to form his or her expert opinion. If the Prosecution is not able or willing to provide us with the sought material that we asked Ms. Tabeau about at the transcript reference I read, we believe they have not complied with this jurisprudence. Further, from the Milosevic case, Decision on admission of expert report of Robert Donia, 15 February 2007. Also from the Milosevic case, Decision on Defence expert witnesses of 21 August, 2007, and from the Stanisic and Simatovic case, Decision on Prosecution submission of the expert report of Nena Tromp and Christian Nielsen, pursuant to Rule 94 bis, dated 18 March, 2008 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Dated 18 March 2008. The jurisprudence reads: "The sources for the report must be clearly indicated and accessible in order to allow the other party or the Trial Chamber to test or challenge the bases on which the expert witness reached his or her conclusions." Again, if the Prosecution, after all these months, is unwilling or unable to give the Defence access to what specific criteria were used by Dr. Tabeau to match purported victims, they have not complied with this jurisprudence. We would ask for a date certain to be provided that material by the Prosecution so that we don't have to keep waiting and hoping and getting different answers from them every time we ask about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am not and have not been directly involved in this issue. I'm rising in the hope of being able to offer a constructive and efficient solution to the repeated interventions and demands. So let me just say the following: Let me begin with the fact that the heat of any submission is not necessarily -- does not necessarily correspond to its accuracy. The Prosecution has provided everything that it has been asked to provide and we say that from the outset. Mr. File has repeated it more than once, we are more than happy under these circumstances to look at all the submissions that were made in the course of today and in relation to this issue to see if there is any way of satisfying the -- a legitimate Defence concern, but as the Court has heard, the Prosecution provided its full response to the list of items prepared by the Defence and submitted to the Prosecution in anticipation of this witness's visit. Until this point, we did not hear any indication that there was any problem in that response. Now, we understand that the submission itself did not reflect the specific item that is the subject of these repeated interventions. My own understanding is that no such item of that type is in existence. Whether or not there is some way of resolving the underlying concerns in a way that advances the efficiency of the proceedings, I don't know, but we're happy to look at during the course of the day and address the Defence and the Court tomorrow. I only rise to say two things. Number one, that there has been no failure on the part of the Prosecution to produce materials for which it has been asked. And, secondly, we are always prepared to consider legitimate requests by the Defence and any requests by the Court to see if it can possibly be fulfilled and that's what we will be doing in the course of this day and responding to the Court to about tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I don't know maybe from the way the problem has been placed it may well, be that some things may have fallen through the cracks. As I understand Mr. Ivetic's position, this request was not made directly to the Prosecution but rather was made to Mrs. Tabeau while on the witness stand and she was asked if she can provide the criteria on which she does her matching, upon which she is alleged to have responded, I do not have it, but it -- I can make it, I can -- it can be done so -- and the request was: Please do. And the idea beings that she would do it later after she had gotten off the stand and then provide it. I stand corrected, Mr. Ivetic, if I misunderstand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You understand me perfectly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So that's why I say, this might have fallen through the cracks because it wasn't directly to you as the Prosecution, it was to the witness herself. And I think if I -- if I become generous to Mr. Ivetic's approach, he is -- I assume he is saying, having heard that request, you as the person whose witness that is, can't you facilitate that we get that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: On this, Your Honour, I'd have to defer to those who worked more directly on this subject and/or with Dr. Tabeau, but my understanding, based on both today and the discussions that arose, and previous general discussions about this, would be the following. Number one, that there was no existing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- log of that type.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ms Tabeau said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Number two, it would be the replication of a process that would basically -- the repetition of the process of doing that, which I understand to be a bizarrely labour-intensive process to the extent that it would actually be -- I would think, if my understanding about this is correct, impossible to actually recreate that process which is so labour-intensive. In other words, you could do the process again but that would never be a way of identifying the particular items that you looked at at a particular time to make the matches. It would be something equivalent to saying, I know the sources you relied upon to reach your opinion, thank you for providing that, but I'd like to know which paragraph of which page you were looking at when you wrote this particular part of your report previously. And so, again, that's my general understanding of the logistical and lack of feasibility [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I hear that explanation. Unfortunately, that's not what Ms. Tabeau said. She said that it can be done -- and just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me correct myself. I'm being advised by my colleagues that Ms. Tabeau said it can be done but she never promised that she would do it. So to that extent, I don't remember that detail but I just remember that this was discussed in court so it may very well that she never promised to give this but she just said that it can be done and it would take a lot of time. So at that point I don't know if we can look at the transcript of that date to see whether she did promise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will verify, exactly, the history because we are all relying on our memories which are not -- perhaps may not be correct. So, therefore, we'll verify all that and then further look at the matter. There's one tiny little thing. Do I understand that there was an additional disclosure today of a document to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Purely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's a yes. Was there an obligation to disclose this? Is it -- do we have to consider it as late disclosure or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: No, it was disclosed purely as a courtesy. It's not -- there was no obligation to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Because late disclosure, where there existed a disclosure obligation, I think according to the Rules you should disclose that to the Chamber as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Just to clarify, the document was only generated last week and it was just a demonstrative exhibit for cross-examination, so there was no obligation there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that's being verified. Let's move on quickly. Ms. Radovanovic, you were a witness, but then in a different sense of some procedural debates where we are here, first of all, to hear your testimony. So we will now continue to hear your testimony. Mr. File will proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'm going to ask you about some of the other information that you referred to when discussing combat. On direct examination, at transcript page 43680 to -83, and then at 43687 to -89, the Judges asked you several questions about the nine documents that you cited at footnote 17 of your report for the proposition that: "There had been armed conflicts." I have just a couple of additional questions for you about those documents. One of them is about timing, in the context of Dr. Tabeau's report. Now, you probably noticed in Dr. Tabeau's report - for the record, P7449 - I'm specifically referring to English pages 18 to 21 and B/C/S pages 22 to 26, Dr. Tabeau provided statistics on when the Tomasica identified victims were reported to have gone missing. And the vast majority, at least 237 out of 378, went missing in July 1992. She put that in Table 12 of her report which is English page 18, B/C/S page 22. And then she broke it down more closely and you could see that the vast majority of those, at least 221, disappeared between 20 and 25 July 1992 and that was Table 14C and Figure 4. So my question for you is: Are you aware that, of the nine documents that you refer to in your report at footnote 17, only one of them is from July 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, would you not speak aloud when questions are put to the witness. Mr. Mladic. Would you stop speaking aloud. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Only one of those documents is from July 1992 or even describes any events of any kind in the entire month of July 1992. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood your question. Are you asking me whether in the documents I cite only one is from July 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I accept it at your word. I know there are several documents. They relate to July and to some other dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: No, there's one document that relates to July; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know it by heart. I would have to check. But I've attached all these documents. I really can't remember now if there is only one relating to July, but I accept it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or perhaps in the break I can check.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I don't think the Defence is going do dispute this point, so I'm going to show you the one which is from July, which is 65 ter 02696. So as you can see, this is a 1 KK combat report to the Main Staff dated 27 July 1992. And if you go to paragraph 2, you can see a reference to the Prijedor area. It says: "Units in the Prijedor region continue operations to find and neutralize groups of extremists." Then if you go to paragraph 5, it says: "We have no information that there have been any losses since the last report." So, in terms of the presence or absence of combat, one thing that you know from this document is that no one in the VRS is suffering casualties here; right? There's no report of that.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the VRS, I don't know. Probably. If they have no documents that there were no losses on the VRS side, then that's probably true.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And you also don't know whether the 1 KK units that are performing operations to find and neutralize groups of extremists are encountering any resistance; right? That's not listed here either?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The previous question said that there: "In terms of presence or absence of combat one thing that you know from this document is that no one in the VRS is suffering casualties here; right? There is no report of that." Item 5 in the English language and in the B/C/S language, that's what I've just checked, says: "We have no information that there have been any losses since the last report." Therefore, what counsel is presenting is an interpretation of the document that -- which does not flow from the plain meaning of the document and is twisting the factual scenario to make a proposition that does not flow from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: That's purely an argumentive objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It indeed is, and ... whether it is twisting the factual scenario, it may be incomplete where it does not give all the details about when the last report was there, but, again, that's a matter not to raise as an objection but you could have raised in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, Mr. Ivetic. I gave you my ruling. I have a question for the witness. Witness, do you when the previous report was issued prior to the one you relied on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember now whether I attached the previous one and this one, but I know what's written in item 1. It's proof that there was combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look at item 1 of this report, it says: "During the night and in the morning, the enemy occasionally fired on our forces. The fire from the direction of Bugojno," et cetera, et cetera. "... was particularly long." So, in my view, there was combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At least in the locations described here. Is that -- how far is that from Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say how far it is from Prijedor, but there are reports that name places close to Prijedor or belong to the Prijedor area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was about this document, not about other documents. Mr. File, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm still on my feet. Given your ruling, I need the guidance and instruction of this Chamber. Is it Your Honours' position that where I rise to object that counsel's question misstates the contents of a document and therefore misstates the evidence upon which he is relying that that is argumentive and should not be raised as an objection and should be dealt with in re-direct. I want Your Honours' ruling on that, so I can understand your previous ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think I have ruled on it, that it may have been incomplete and that the terms in which it was phrased made it more argumentive than necessary to object to the question. I leave it to that. Please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Just for the record, Your Honour, the previous combat report from this corps from the previous day is already in evidence at P248.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So something else that you don't know from this document is whether the 1 KK units that are performing operations to find and neutralize groups of extremists are encountering any resistance.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see it is known. It's under item 1. That's how I understand this document. My entire objection was that Dr. Tabeau was able to see from a variety of documents that there had been combat, so she cannot claim that all of these are executions, which is the insinuation she makes; namely, executions as part of a campaign of ethnic cleansing.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Are you not aware that these locations in Item 1 are not in Prijedor -- not even close to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this document, possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So this document then can change the geography of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you something else about this document. You can't tell -- and now I'm specifically referring to item 2. You can't tell from that item whether the so-called extremists are even armed; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not my purpose to determine that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Can you --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that nobody is fighting or firing from nothing. I don't know whether they were armed. I suppose they were. If there were all sorts of actions during the night, I suppose the people were not unarmed, but I don't know for a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's just assume for the sake of argument that item 1 is not relevant to this issue. If you look just at item 2, there's nothing there that suggests that these so-called extremists are armed; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if that's the way you look at it, yes. But the purpose of my conclusions was to determine not whether they were armed or not but whether there was fighting or not, and there are various documents testifying to it. Not only this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. File, that the expert witness has emphasised importance of looking at the possibility that people may have died in combat. We look at the matter in the totality of the evidence. The witness has drawn our attention to a few documents relating to certain places, to certain dates, and I think whether this would support or compel any conclusion that this would give data which I find irrelevant is still to be considered, but perhaps not very useful to go into detail on this matter with this expert witness at this moment. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, paragraph 2 cited to by Mr. File indicates units were returning fire. In my plain understanding of the English language that means both parties were armed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on. We have heard your argument in relation to how we should understand this document. It's on the record. Please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Thank you. And I would just as that it's referring to their own units --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I said, as a matter of fact, that it's argument, that's an implicit hint to not argue at this moment, but, rather, ask questions to a witness. Therefore, there's also no need to respond in an arguing way. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: You mentioned another document in your report and in your testimony, which was the 2002 report by Nicolas Sebire. I'm going ask you some questions about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Before I do, I would like to tender document 02696 that we were just looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit P7828, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And for the record, you testified about this document we're going to look at pages 43679 -681 -685, and -686. So this will be 65 ter 26260. So as this is coming up, you'll see this is a 28 August 2002 report by Nicolas Sebire entitled: Additional report, exhumations and proof of death, municipality of Prijedor. You listed this as one of the sources you consulted in preparing your report and you quoted this document in paragraph 25 of your report. You recall that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And Your Honours as we noted earlier, the main text of this report along with Annex 1 and Annex 15 are in evidence as P3282 and I'll be using some additional parts, so for simplicity, I'm using the complete report which is uploaded under 2620 and I'll alert the Chamber when we begin to use pages that are not already in evidence. If we could go to e-court English page 7 and B/C/S page 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you verified whether the confidentiality which is claimed on the cover page whether that has any consequences for our proceedings and not only for the portions that are already in evidence but perhaps also for the portions perhaps still to be added?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I don't believe -- I have -- I have checked whether it is under seal, but I don't believe there are currently confidentiality concerns but when I get to pages that may have that, I will alert everyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please keep this in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So under heading 3.2, the documentation relating to the proof of death --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Sorry, I've just been notified it is under seal so I think it is not for broadcast, this part. It's due to the annexes which contain names, that's why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, I do not know -- I have no clear recollection of which annexes have caused this. It's a non-public document for the time being. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So under this heading, it says the documentation relating to the proof of death. It says: "The Office of the Prosecutor has received from the Bosnian authorities court judgements concerning declarations of death for 2.026 individuals" --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't follow you. You are reading from the document of Nicolas Sebire?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I think we need the previous page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File is reading 3.2 which is on the top left side where it reads "dokumentacija." You found it? Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
