utterances.text: It says: "The Office of the Prosecutor has received from the Bosnian authorities court judgements concerning declarations of death for 2.026 individuals from the municipalities of Prijedor, Sanski Most, Banja Luka, Bosanski Novi, Bosanska Dubica, Kljuc, Kotor Varos, and Donji Vakuf, who were killed or went missing during the 1992 to 1995 conflict. All of the individuals for whom proof of their death was received are non-Serbs. This report will only focus on those declared officially deceased from the municipality of Prijedor, and therefore concern 1.295 individuals." And there's a footnote that says: "Including those declared officially deceased and exhumed since then." "In general" -- if we could go to the next page in English "these court decisions are accompanied by a birth or marriage certificate in respect of the individual to be declared officially dead. The decisions mainly rely on the testimonies of relatives or witnesses who were in a position to state when a particular individual was last seen alive." Now, when you were testifying at page 43664, you said the only source that's "official for use in demographic scientific work" is the death registry which includes "a court decision declaring a specific person dead." And then you criticised Dr. Tabeau for not using court decisions in her analysis, and that was page 43685. So when you saw this report relating to court decisions in Prijedor from 1992 to 1995, or governing people who died or went missing during that period, that must have been something that you were interested in; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is very interesting, for the simple reason that he is here using official documents n mortality and he says there is a database on it. It's not only the court decisions. I've said that there also death certificates.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Let's look at the information about the database as it is described here. It is English page 8 and the same page in the B/C/S, page 9. It's under the heading 3.3, the databases. In says in the second paragraph on the --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you put the tenth page in Serbian on the screen? I see only the subheading on the ninth page.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We're still in the right place. It's going to be the second paragraph under the heading: 3.3, the databases. Okay?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: It says: "As it was impossible to translate all of the documentation, two databases were created and bilingual (Bosnian-Croatian-Serbian/English) data entry clerks were brought in to enter the information. These two persons were responsible for summarising the documentation provided by the Bosnian authorities and entering the information in the English language into the databases. The present report relies on the information that has been entered into the databases according to the above-mentioned procedure." And then there are headings below that will show the two databases. 3.3.1, which you see on the screen, is the exhumation database, which we're not going to look at for the moment, and if we go to the next page in the English and in the B/C/S, under the heading 3.3.2, it says the proof of death database. And the first paragraph here says: "This is the database that contains all the information received by the Office of the Prosecutor and relating to the court decisions made by either the Sanski Most or Kljuc Municipal Courts declaring missing persons from the ARK as officially deceased." That's the database that you were just talking about; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But there's part where Mr. Nicolas Sebire precisely cites Prijedor and the court decisions for Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We're going to get to that. If we can go to English page 13 and B/C/S page 15. So here we've arrived at the passage that you quoted in your report. Under heading 4.2 which is titled: The court decisions issued by the Bosnian municipal courts, I'm going to read the first paragraph of this and then I'm going ask you a question about it. It says: "Court rulings relating to the municipality of Prijedor were received by the Office of the Prosecutor for 1.295 individuals. The large majority of these individuals are Bosnian Muslims. It should be mentioned that the court rulings concern individuals who were still missing at the time the court decision was issued. In some instances, individuals officially declared dead have been exhumed and identified since then and must therefore be excluded when discussing the rulings. Out of 1.295 court rulings, 1.054 individuals were killed or went missing in the course of the year 1992." And next to the figure 1.054 there's a footnote that says: "See Annex 5 which lists all 1.055 individuals. Continuing on in the paragraph it says: "However, 99 cases out of 1.054 have been excluded from the analysis. For those 100 cases, the information contained into the court ruling indicates that the individuals were killed in the course of a combat action or that there is doubt about the time and circumstances of the death or disappearance." This is what you were talking about when you said in your report at paragraph 25: "The fact that sources contain court rulings of death existing in a Demographic Unit have been discarded without any explanation having been given for not using them in the report of 20 August 2014, gives rise to a reasonable suspicion these documents are being ignored in a calculated manner." Now, this is the report and these are the court rulings that you were referring to; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Note that there's a footnote that says: "See Annex 5," which I just mentioned, which lists all 1.055 individuals. I also note that the B/C/S version says "all 1.005," I believe. So what this document is telling you is that the report contains an annex that listed over a thousand people who went missing in Prijedor in 1992 and that on that list are 99 people who either may have been killed in combat or for whom there was doubt about the circumstances of death or disappearance. So for someone who places great stock in court decisions and who raises this possibility that there could have been combat fatalities, this must have looked like a useful resource to you. Did you check the annexes to see if you could find anyone from the Tomasica victim list there?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not my purpose. My goal was to show that the doctor had at least to hint that all the persons who she claims were exhumed from Tomasica were not executed but that it's likely that they were killed in combat. It's unimportant whether among the 99 persons there may be someone from Dr. Tabeau's list, for me. What was important for me was to show that even when she had documents at her disposal, she did not check them but did not mention them at all. So Dr. Tabeau does not mention this database as one that she consulted at least. If she had mentioned it and said, I have checked it and determined that it wasn't there, that would have been about a different matter, but she doesn't mention it in her data sources, she doesn't say a single word about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just verify the -- you are interpreted as having said, Professor Radovanovic, that Dr. Tabeau had at least to hint that all the persons who were exhumed from Tomasica were not executed but that it's likely that some of them were killed in combat. Is that what you said? Or did you intend to say what she should have hinted at that not all the persons who were exhumed from Tomasica were executed but that it's likely that some of them were killed in combat? Is it the latter that you intended to say or ... did you say that she should have hinted at that not all the persons were executed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that she had to hint that it wasn't an execution where she says at the end as part of an ethnic cleansing campaign but that there is a possibility that some of the persons may have been killed in combat. Because it's evident that there was fighting going on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then one follow-up question. If there's fighting going on, does that mean at least some of those were killed in combat or is that also just a possibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She hints at the possibility and she cannot determine whether it is certain or not, but she also cannot assert that all the persons found in Tomasica perished in an ethnic cleansing campaign. That's precisely what Dr. Tabeau claims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Although that was not my question, please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So I asked whether you checked the annexes. You said that was not my purpose, so I take that as a no, you didn't check them.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. Because I never intended to check whether someone from Dr. Tabeau's list was present here. The goal was to show that she never took into account an existing source. Why? She could have said, well, it exists but I do not use it because it does not contain what I need.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So you felt it was important to raise the question about what was in this source that you were looking at, but if I quote you, you say it's unimportant whether among the 99 persons there may be someone from Dr. Tabeau's list. So, for you, it is important to raise the question but not to know the answer. That's what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would object to the question because in the question he says, "but if I quote you," and then he say something that I have not been able to find in the answer of the witness. So if he's going to quote the witness, he has to quote the witness verbatim. And I don't see where the witness said in the answer to the last question anything that says it is unimportant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I assist you, Mr. Ivetic, to find the relevant sentence. Page 70, line 25. I quote: "It's unimportant whether among the 99 persons there may be someone from Dr. Tabeau's list." That is, in my understanding, the sentence Mr. File was referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, this being verified now what the witness exactly said, perhaps you repeat your question following on the quote which was very accurately pronounced by my colleague.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I said that for me it was not important because I established the source rather than whether someone is in the list or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. So the same question: For you, it is important to raise the question but it is not important to know the answer.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is important to show that Dr. Tabeau, even when relevant sources for determining mortality are available to her, does not use them without providing an explanation why.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. File. Mr. Ivetic, could you give us an indication, I asked about it yesterday, about how much time you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At this stage I would think about 25, 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we might even find a little bit of time to deal with a few procedural issues as well. But perhaps it's better that we take the break now and then start at 1.30 and then you have an uninterrupted.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes? We take a break. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes, Professor Radovanovic. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Although the witness may be prepared to be on stand by, I briefly deal with the following matter that's tendering of contextual evidence. On 21st of April of this year, the Chamber denied admission into evidence of documents bearing Rule 65 ter numbers 30547 and 33653, as the Prosecution had not specifically set out why it should be allowed to tender those documents prior to the rebuttal phase. The Chamber invited the Prosecution to make submissions as to why it should be permitted to tender the documents at this stage. On the 26th of April, the Prosecution made oral submissions which the Chamber understands to have been in response to the 21st of April invitation. On the 28th of April, the Defence responded. The Chamber notes that the Prosecution has not made submissions specific to the documents in question. The Chamber finds that the Prosecution has not specifically set out why it should be allowed to tender specifically these documents during the Defence case rather than at the rebuttal phase and will not revisit its denial of their admission into evidence. That's -- if the witness is ready, she can ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Radovanovic, you'll now be re-examined by Mr. Ivetic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Professor, at transcript page 43.871 through 43.872, you offered to explain, if not clear enough as to paragraph 13 of your report but you were not allowed to do so. To give you the context, I will read that portion of the transcript for you, starting at line 10 on page 43.871. And it reads as follows: "Q. You referred to paragraph 13 and footnote 2 of your report. In paragraph 13, you say: 'In a publication intended for the broad public, the Prosecution expert witness observes in reference to the reports of demographers engaged by the Office of the Prosecutor that whenever a demographic expert report is admitted" -- and then you intervened: "A. I cannot follow you. You are reading from paragraph 13, right? "Q. Yes, I'll continue. 'The likely consequence is that the report has impact on the judgement in contrast to reports from the opposite side, although a vast majority of the work of Defence experts unfortunately cannot be seen as up to international scientific standards.' So this reference that you made also does not describe the known and recognised international standards that you refer to; correct? "A. Well, that's a quotation. I cannot describe it. I am quoting Dr. Tabeau who is an expert in demography and who is competent to judge what are and aren't internationally recognised standards. And if Dr. Tabeau did not quote it from a textbook, I thought it was absurd for me to quote it but, again, I repeat, I can explain it if it is not clear enough." Then the following question was: "Q. Well, just to be clear, the only source that you refer to, according to you, in your report as justification for what the international standards in statistics and demography are is the Prosecution expert; right? "A. No. If you allow me, I have a Ph.D. in demography and I surely know what are international standards and what are not. I suppose that since Dr. Tabeau is the same, she knows it as well, and she needs not explain to another expert in her field. I didn't think I should cite textbooks because I am an expert and I'm the most qualified in demography in this courtroom. If somebody finds something incorrect, inaccurate in my report, please go ahead. I do not think I need to cite textbooks but I'm ready and willing to explain." And did you have anything further you felt that you needed to explain in relation to this question, professor.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can only add, as that was obviously not clear, that Dr. Tabeau does not quote anything anywhere in her report when she says what are the relevant official documents for mortality, and those are certificates of death and certificates of birth and court rulings, and that is undisputed. I think that everyone working in demographics knows that. That's what I tried to say. If Dr. Tabeau never quotes anything anywhere, then I don't know why I am requested to quote textbooks and I am in discussion with a demographer who knows a lot about this. Perhaps I should have quoted it for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, but I quoted Dr. Tabeau who says what the reports are. So, in my report, it's a quotation, and I have nothing against it. I'm just proving that she knows what international standards and sources for draws conclusions about mortality are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you refer to 43.871 through -72. For me, it's 891, -92. That's at least what I have in my e-court. I don't know whether you have the same e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm looking at the transcript that was sent to us by the transcript service and I'm reading from the actual page that says 43.872. I don't know if it's not the e-court, it's the Word version since I don't have access to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to know there may be some confusion there. Let's leave it to that at this moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in relation to a question posed by Judge Orie at -- and I have it as transcript pages 43.876, line 16 through 43.877, line 9, you said that you couldn't agree with Judge Orie so I'd like to read the question to you and ask you to explain your answer to us. And it reads as follows: "Judge Orie: I'll cut this matter short. It's clear that the totals include the unavailable. It seems also clear that in the percentages, the unavailable were excluded, which is not a very transparent way of presenting these tables. It also explains why the 13.2 per cent should be taken out if you want to present the ethnicity of those for whom the ethnicity is an available datum. If you want to present something else, that is, that you wasn't to present that the percentage of Muslims is on the total, that is, available ethnicity, not available ethnicity then, of course, the percentages are different. Would you agree with that? "The witness" -- This is you. "I don't know what Dr. Tabeau means. I see what she writes -- I really don't know, I can't -- And then Judge Orie: "I'm asking if you agree with that I said, which includes some criticism on Dr. Tabeau because she is not consistent but I tried to explain what you could understand from this and I wondered whether you agreed with me and if you want to re-read it then, well, no you can't, well, in English you can re-read it." And then the answer as given by you, professor, is recorded as being: "No I can't agree with you for the simple reason that ..." And then were interrupted. And I wanted to see if you could provide us with an explanation of your answer and a continuation of what you were going to say before you were interrupted, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall. If there is a total mass representing 100 per cent and you have certain elements within the total mass, then you work in relation to the total mass. For Dr. Tabeau, the total mass is 378. And she notes, I have found that there are Muslim, Serbs, Croats, and unknown. If she reduces the total mass, even though it exists, then she can increase the percentage of one of the ethnicities, in this case, Muslims. So you have to have a reason why you want to drop something that exists. You cannot just say well, drop it. So if she operates with one mass, then the mass has to be constant. She cannot say well, for me, 378 represented 100 per cent but let's drop out the -- those who are unknown. The unknown exist. If you leave them out, then 100 per cent is no longer 378 but when you subtract those who are unknown. So that is why I did not agree with His Honour Judge Orie. Dr. Tabeau could have done that differently. She could have left that out or dropped it but then the total mass could not be 100 per cent but, for example, 90 per cent and then in a footnote she could have said the difference to 100 per cent is constituted by those whose ethnicity is unknown, and that is how this is supposed to be done professionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Professor, we have heard from the Prosecutor that there does not exist a log of the matching results obtained by Dr. Tabeau when she performed matching according to whatever criteria as to Tomasica. From the standpoint of the science of demography, what comment do you have as to that admission by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that as beyond the scope of cross-examination. I didn't ask her any questions about logs or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is new material that came to us after we -- after we completed our direct examination. I believe it's a highly relevant matter to consider. It was a matter that we had asked previously and had not gotten a firm answer on and we were just told by Mr. Tieger when he stood up, I believe it was in the last session and told us on the record so I believe I'm entitled to get this expert's opinion as to what that means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, although the objection and response are on cross-purposes, we allow you to put the question to the witness, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Professor, let's me please re-read my question to you. We have heard today from the Prosecutor that there does not exist a log of the matching results obtained by Dr. Tabeau when she performed matching according to whatever criteria as to Tomasica. From the standpoint of the science of demography, what comment do you have as to that admission by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if there is no log, how did she perform the matching? So that means that she can perform the matching in any way she wants. She has to show us the criteria because once she begins the matching, she has to set the condition for a match and say, I'm going to look for this, this and this, from one source, in another one. And I really can't believe that there is no log of the matching, unless Dr. Tabeau decided to match in any way she wanted and then she could say, well, this is matched and this is it not. I don't know a single professional who would do the matching without setting the criteria and hold on to them so that he would know the next day or five days later that this is used for that in the procedure. I don't know what it means when it is said that there is no log of matching results. Because one cannot remember that, keep it in one's head. It is something that has to be noted down somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My next question has to do with 65 ter number 33791 which you were shown during cross-examination, and I'd ask for that to be shown on the screen, just to refresh your recollection as to what we're talking about. It's the November 2015 new memorandum or report of Dr. Tabeau which was not introduced in evidence. So in relation to this report, you were answering a question at temporary transcript page 15, line 24 to temporary transcript page 16, line 9, earlier today, and you were not allowed to complete your answer. I will read for you the relevant transcript of your answer and then ask you to please complete what you were about to say. It reads as follows: "A. I don't think I would change anything except perhaps that she is putting in what doesn't even exist yet at the time she is writing the report, but it doesn't change the whole total. Dr. Tabeau made new calculations every year. If I had been receiving that month by month, then it would have been all right. She has another correction, I believe, from 2015 to the total number that I have seen here in The Hague, but that's a correction to the total number, and now she says it is no longer 378 but it's -- so these corrections Dr. Tabeau is making here now do not affect the overall result because" -- And, professor, this is where you were cut off, and I'd ask for you, if possible, to recreate your answer and complete your answer.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They do not affect the whole because there are no changes to the whole, or perhaps because changes are subsequent, they do not affect the entirety based on which I make my conclusions. In August 2013, Dr. Tabeau knew that these people would all be identified by November 2015 and then she proves it in November 2015. I say again, in this report, she did not change the total number. She had already concluded it in 2013. She received information from the ICMP that all these people would be identified, or were identified, but she seems to have known it already years before. That seems a bit odd to me, but there's nothing I can do about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to ask you about the PowerPoint hypothetical that you were shown relating to students and that has now been introduced as P7827.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can call up that exhibit and show the last page of the same so that the professor can understand what document we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now we have it on the screen. So this is what we're talking about. And I'd like to ask you, professor, in your opinion, can such a hypothetical example be used to describe the matching of persons with missing person lists and the census?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because Dr. Tabeau is not matching the census according to the ID with any other document. ID in the census would perhaps be the unique identification number, and she doesn't have the unique ID number in any of the documents she is using for Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at -- in relation to the list that you prepared which is D1464 - which should not be broadcast - at temporary transcript page 27, lines 2 through 7, you were asked if you considered that Rakovcani was in Prijedor and you started to answering by saying: "Yes, I did consider that possibility because" ... And then you were cut off, and I'd like to ask you to complete that answer if you remember it.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Census records precisely the place of birth. Based on a document you have your personal ID. I don't know how precisely that is recorded by the ICRC. It is usually provided by the family. But I don't know if the family member knows that, whether he knows the place of birth, but I suppose he does. So I guarantee for the datum in the census and the ICRC, considering that nobody checks it, it is possible that anyone can come in and provide information, not necessarily a family member, I don't know if the data is correct. But if that is so, if the data is not accurate, then the ICRC is not reliable. That's not the source on which you check mortality anywhere in the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At today's transcript page 44, line 12, through page 45, line 3, you were asked a question, and I'd like to read to you that portion of the transcript, and then I'll ask you to give your full answer. "Judge Orie: Let's -- let me there again stop you. You asked for something in writing. Two months later, you're in The Hague, you haven't received it, do I understand your answer well, that you say, I didn't ask for it because I felt already that it was intentionally kept away from me and, therefore, I didn't ask for it again? Is that how we have to understand your answer? "The Witness: If you send something to somebody in writing and if it's on record" -- and then your answer was interrupted. And Judge Orie said: "Would you please answer my question." And then it continues: "The witness: In any case, I don't think it's accidental." Can I ask you to try to complete the answer that you were in the process of giving in relation to this question, if you remember it.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do remember. If you are seeking criteria and Dr. Tabeau says I'll provide it, if I request the criteria in writing and I suppose when Dr. Tabeau gives me what I have asked for in writing, she holds in her hand the list, there are only two possibilities. Either she is sloppy or she is intentionally keeping it away from me. I cannot say now definitely that it was intentional. I have no proof, but I believe it was not done in the way it should have. You have in your hands a list. The Defence is requesting it. I will either give it to them or I will put it in a footnote and explain why I didn't. Let me had, I received a database that contains ten elements and in the report from 2010, she states that this database contains 12 elements, but I did not make a fuss. Why do I see ten elements and she says there are 12? I thought, perhaps, it doesn't matter. But about this, I did make a fuss because I requested to receive in writing the criteria according to which Dr. Tabeau says that she – she doesn't always do matching according to the same criteria, there are some additional ones, et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You were asked in cross-examination about the Popovic case and when you visited the ICTY to review demography records in that case. Thinking now back to the Popovic case, did Dr. Tabeau and the Prosecutor give you access to everything that you sought at that time to be reviewed?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I had no objections, then probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Professor, I thank you for your patience. The Defence has no further questions for you at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have before I give an opportunity to Mr. File. In the Popovic case, was there a log on how the matchings were made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. File, I just wanted to know whether it was there. Please proceed. Further Cross-examination by Mr. File:

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just three final questions. When you were talking about what was provided or not provided, regarding the 2009 ICRC list, You were aware, retire, that the 2009 list contains the information from the 2005 list as well; right? The 2009 list is an update?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I fail to see how this arises from my re-direct. I have not asked a single question about the ICRC list in my re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: He asked about what she had available at the time, and I think this is perfectly reasonable as a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At what time? I did not ask a question about what she had available at the time. That is not in my re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please give the exact ...

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: He asked at transcript page 84: "Can I ask you to try to complete the answer that you were in the process of giving in relation to this question, if you remember it." And the question was, from Judge Orie: "You asked for something in writing, two months later you were in The Hague, you haven't received it, do I understand your answer well," and it goes on. In the context of that question, in cross-examination, was the ICRC list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Objection is granted. Please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you testified that -- when you testified -- pardon me. You said at temporary transcript, page 80: "Well, if there's no log, how did she perform the matching? So that means that she can perform the matching in any way she wants. She has to show us the criteria." Do you consider the criteria for matching and the log to be the same thing?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it's the same thing. You record a criterion according to which you match something.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So you've never heard of a log where every decision that's made on a particular match is written down, recorded, sometimes thousands of times. You don't consider that to be a log or you're not aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I fail to see the relevance of this since it's -- the Prosecution has said they don't have this. If they are now saying they do have this, we have another issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Ivetic, the issue is how relevant, how important a log is and that's an issue whether or not we have it is not the relevant issue. Could you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a log on 72 criteria and that's what I saw. As to what Dr. Tabeau says later about additional criteria she used to make adjustments, for that, there is no log. At least I haven't seen one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My final question is related to your comment at transcript page 77, line 3, you say: "If Dr. Tabeau never quotes anything anywhere, then I don't know why I am requested to quote textbooks and I'm in discussion with a demographer who knows a lot about this." Just to clarify your comment there, are you saying that Dr. Tabeau never quotes any scholarly sources or any professional or academic articles in her reports?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I meant to say that Dr. Tabeau, when she says but the documents according to which mortality is recorded, she doesn't say any books because that's known; whereas in some reports and some articles she used, there are citations. So she doesn't cite what is generally known in the science of demographics.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. File. This then concludes, Professor Radovanovic, your testimony. I would like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague a long way and to be here for quite a number of days and for having answered all the questions that were put to you, put to you by the parties, put to you by the Bench. I would like to thank you, and I wish you a safe return home again. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are five minutes away from the usual time where we adjourn. I have approximately one and a half, two pages of small items to deal with, procedural issues. If the parties would agree that we extend the session slightly so that we avoid coming back tomorrow morning. I'm looking at both Defence and Prosecution to start with. And then, of course, also whether interpreters, security all those who are constantly assisting us would have any problem. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, of course, we have no objection to extending the session. I'd actually risen on a slightly different issue which was just to make sure that we correctly understand the state of play as to requests for material after the conclusion of Ms. Radovanovic's testimony which is, as we understand it, first everybody is in agreement there is no matching log that could ever have been provided. The Defence requested a list of criteria, we provided the one with we had and there's nothing else in existence that can be provided and that's the situation we're in. If there's any dispute about that, I'd just ask Mr. Ivetic to confirm my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There is dispute. What has been provided is dated from the 2013 Srebrenica report. It does not relate to Tomasica. I don't know how criteria that existed in 2013 and results obtained in 2013 can relate to results that Dr. Tabeau says she did in 2014. I don't know that. Dr. Tabeau in her testimony indicated that she, for every single project she did when specifically asked about Tomasica, there were additional criteria that she created based on the logic of the 72 keys. Those additional criteria that she used exist, albeit perhaps only in her head maybe not on paper, but they exist. They were used for the Tomasica report. We are entitled to have them. That's what we are asking for. We have never received anything that comports to that additional criteria that Dr. Tabeau testified under oath that she used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your position is that whatever is in the head of an expert and if it has played a role in drafting a report should be made available. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- your position. Thank you. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I don't think it will come as a surprise that we disagree with that position, Your Honour. Separately in both Dr. Tabeau and Dr. Radovanovic have said at points in their testimony that it would be either incredibly difficult and time-consuming or entirely impossible to create such a list after the process was over. My -- and would basically require redoing all the matches, and that comes, as I understand it, because this is -- because of the way matching works, and we saw a little bit during Dr. Radovanovic's examination. So during the hypothetical exercise, it turned out that a student who wrote J126 could be confirmed as John Eliot Smith 125 and the criteria there was basically a judgement call based on the fact that the other examples had been blocked. But to do that for every instance, you would have to redo all the matching. Now, in terms what's been available, Dr. Tabeau repeatedly invited Mr. Ivetic during her testimony to ask about specific examples as the Chamber also underscored at the time, and Dr. Radovanovic and her team came to The Hague, used our systems, had access to all of the same information and could test Dr. Tabeau's evidence additionally by attempting to check her work, by seeing if they could recreate the matches or came to different results. Now, if the Defence wants to assert that the lack of a complete -- what's now sort of in a middle ground between a log and a list of criteria goes the weight to be afforded to Dr. Tabeau's testimony, that's something they can do, and the Chamber will have to assess that in the context of all the other evidence on the record. That's very different from suggesting that there's a disclosure obligation for everything in an expert's head while they're preparing a report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There are many, many things mixed in here. I will try to address them all, but first I will also say that as to the issue of extending the session, the Defence has not have an objection since we will likely do so in the midst of my response. First and foremost, I have cited to Your Honours jurisprudence from prior cases of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll verify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I -- I -- I expect nothing less. That jurisprudence relates to the transparency of expert reports and ability of opposing party to have access to the materials that the expert relied upon in reaching their conclusions. Therefore, if the Prosecution and Dr. Tabeau are unable to provide this Chamber and this Defence with the methodology that she employed to create the matches in a format that we can understand, that we can see, that we can verify, it's much more serious than Mr. Traldi sets forth. Because in that case it doesn't go to the weight of the expert testimony. It goes towards its exclusion. And if that is the case, this Defence will move for the expert report of Dr. Tabeau and her related testimony to be stricken from these proceedings, not only as to Tomasica but as to Srebrenica and since now we hear there are no matching records. That is a critical and fundamental violation of the Rule 94 bis jurisprudence. That makes it impossible for this Defence to be able to look at the expert opinions and verify and take issue with them in the way foreseen under the Rules because a party has made a decision not to record their results in such a manner so it can't be verified. In relation to the assertion made by Mr. Traldi, and I want to scroll back on the transcript to make sure that I'm not misquoting it. But at temporary transcript page 90, lines 13 to 18, he is cited as saying the following: "Now in terms of what's been available Dr. Tabeau repeatedly cited to ask about specific examples as the Chamber also underscored at the time, and Dr. Radovanovic and her team came to The Hague, used systems, had access to all of the same information and could test Dr. Tabeau's evidence additionally by attempting to check her work, but seeing if they could recreate the matches to come to different results." There are two points here I'd like to address. One is the specific examples. What Dr. Tabeau asked me was to provide specific sources, which I did, and asked her what criteria she used for each one. As Dr. Radovanovic has testified in these past few days, for work according to the principles of scientific demography, one does not change keys as to sources, and she appraised Dr. Tabeau's offer during my cross-examination as being that she is playing with me. Because the same keys apply to all sources. So that's one comment. Number two, the comment that our team and Dr. Radovanovic had access to all of the same material as the Office of the Prosecutor is patently false. We were given limited access to three linked computers that were set up in the Defence offices of this Tribunal and when I say "we," I mean the Defence expert and her assistants. They were not given access, direct access to the demographic records of the Office of the Prosecutor. Instead, copied on those three computers, which did not have an Internet connection, was material, including some of the material that had been asked for and some material that had not been asked for. We've already heard from Professor Radovanovic that some of the material she would have expected to find and that she had asked for was not on that material. So to say that they had access to everything that Dr. Tabeau had access to, we can't ever know that, because we've never been provided an itinerary, an inventory, of all material, all the sources available in the OTP's demographic database. Dr. Tabeau testified, for instance, that she personally has access and logged onto the ICMP database to do her work. Our experts never had that ability, never had that option to log onto the ICMP database. So the representations by Mr. Traldi on this matter are perhaps too general and do not accurately reflect the totality of the circumstances. Now, I would only add one last point. The hypothetical we looked at which relates to students and ID numbers, respectfully, as we heard Dr. Radovanovic say, has nothing to do with the work that Dr. Tabeau allegedly did with respect to the sources that she examined. It's a red herring. So I don't know why we're constantly going back to that and saying, well, as this demonstrates it can't be said to have demonstrated anything because [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't this an argument in relation to the evaluation of the evidence rather than a response to the matter raised by Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Actually, it's a response to the matter raised by Mr. Traldi, at temporary transcript, page 90 lines 5 through 8, where he specifically talks about what we can draw from the hypothetical example. And so I agree, in a way it is argument. Argument that you've presented the Prosecution the opportunity to give their arguments, and now the Defence would like to make its own arguments, because the same rules should apply to both sides in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is all and I apologise for going over the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I didn't give you a time-limit so, therefore -- The Chamber will consider the matter, and there's a fair chance that we would give a ruling in writing on the matter. We'll still ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If necessary. Of course, that's the first thing we'll have to do is to find out whether we have to decide anything at this very moment. Then, where all parties agreed with a slightly extended session and where -- in order to avoid that we have to come back tomorrow morning, I see that there's a lot of nodding in the affirmative in the booth as well, I'll deal with a few procedural matters. The first one is a remaining issue from the testimonies of Vojo Kupresanin and Jose Cutileiro. On 24 February of last year, Exhibit P7005, excerpts from the 8th Session of the Republika Srpska Assembly, was admitted into evidence through Vojo Kupresanin. On the 9th of December, Jose Cutileiro gave evidence in relation to the speeches given by Karadzic and Krajisnik during the same session. On the 20th of January, 2016, the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence, advising that the two speeches had been added to the extract and uploaded into e-court under 65 ter number 02345B, the Chamber instructs the Registry to replace Exhibit P7005 with the new version and gives the Defence one week do revisit the matter, if necessary. I move onto Exhibit P401, which is an instruction from the RS Presidency and was admitted into evidence on 30 October 2012.
